card.name: Subject or verb in travel and chance narratives
card.fires_on: Small words (it, which, finally, was, been, were) that follow a subject in a historical or natural-history story about journeys, drifting or chance finds. The next word is usually a past-tense verb.

modes.label: Journey narrative
modes.description: Pronoun or adverb inside a story of travel, drifting or migration, right before the verb of arriving.
modes.example: After drifting about for some days,<< it>> finally arrived on the shores of Taneg

modes.label: Chance or happening
modes.description: Linking word in a passage about what happens to someone or is found by chance.
modes.example: Fortune; hap; that<< which>> happens to a person by chance, conceived

modes.label: Auxiliary before a past participle
modes.description: Was, were or been just before a verb like shot, found or repaired.
modes.example: three adult birds of the same kind<< were>> shot near Dennisville in the

card.writes: It slightly favors words like chance and wash, which suggests it nudges the text toward event-style continuations.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in old-fashioned stories of travel, drifting or things found by chance.
